definitions.definition: A word used to identify any of a class of people, places, or things (e.g., Pilot, Airport, Happiness).
A word that can function by itself as a noun phrase and that refers either to the participants in the discourse (e.g., I, you) or to someone or something mentioned elsewhere (e.g., she, it, this).
A word used to describe an action, state, or occurrence (e.g., Fly, Communicate, Is).
A word or phrase naming an attribute, added to or grammatically related to a noun to modify or describe it (e.g., Clear, Professional, Huge).
A word or phrase that modifies or qualifies an adjective, verb, or other adverb, expressing a relation of place, time, circumstance, manner, cause, degree, etc. (e.g., Quickly, Very, Well).
A word governing, and usually preceding, a noun or pronoun and expressing a relation to another word (e.g., On, In, At).
A word used to connect clauses or sentences or to coordinate words in the same clause (e.g., And, But, If).
An abrupt remark, made especially as an aside or interruption (e.g., Ah!, Wow!, Oh!).
A sentence consisting of only one independent clause, with a single subject and predicate.
A sentence containing two or more independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (e.g., for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so).
A sentence containing one independent clause and at least one dependent (subordinate) clause.
A sentence having two or more independent clauses and one or more dependent clauses.
The grammatical rule stating that the subject and verb must agree in number. A singular subject takes a singular verb, and a plural subject takes a plural verb.
Used to describe habits, unchanging situations, general truths, and fixed arrangements.
Used to describe an action that is happening right now or in the near future.
Used to describe an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past or began in the past and continues to the present.
Used to talk about a completed action in a time before now.
Used to talk about things that haven't happened yet.
